title: Critère de platitude par fibres
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$, $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$, $(S',\mathfrak m_{S'})$ be local rings and $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}S\xrightarrow{\beta}S'$ local homomorphisms ($\alpha(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, $\beta(\mathfrak m_S)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S'}$); let $M$ be an $S'$-module, regarded as an $S$-module and an $R$-module by restriction of scalars. Assume (1) $S$ and $S'$ are essentially of finite presentation over $R$: each is isomorphic, as an $R$-algebra (via $\alpha$, resp. $\beta\circ\alpha$), to a localization $W^{-1}B$ of a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$; (2) $M$ is an $S'$-module of finite presentation ($M\cong\operatorname{coker}(S'^{\oplus a}\to S'^{\oplus b})$ for some $a,b\ge0$ and some $S'$-linear map); (3) $M\neq0$; (4) $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ is a flat module over $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (5) $M$ is a flat $R$-module. Then $S$ is flat over $R$ and $M$ is a flat $S$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), 'Critère de platitude par fibres'; its proof reduces to the Noetherian case Lemma 00MP (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian) by writing R as a directed colimit of essentially finite type Z-algebras

proof.text: (Claim L: a localization of a module flat over the base is flat over the base.) Let $A\to C$ be a ring map, $W\subseteq C$ a multiplicative subset and $P$ a $C$-module which is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; let $W^{-1}P$ be its localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], an $A$-module through $A\to C$. Then $W^{-1}P$ is a flat $A$-module. Indeed, let $u:X_1\to X_2$ be an injective $A$-linear map. Since $P$ is flat over $A$, $1_P\otimes u:P\otimes_AX_1\to P\otimes_AX_2$ is injective, and it is $C$-linear for the $C$-module structures through $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] applied to the exact sequence $0\to P\otimes_AX_1\to P\otimes_AX_2$, the map $W^{-1}(1_P\otimes u)$ is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with the ring map $A\to C$, $T=W$, the $C$-module $P$ and the $A$-modules $X_1$, $X_2$) there are isomorphisms $W^{-1}(P\otimes_AX_i)\cong W^{-1}P\otimes_AX_i$, natural in $X_i$, so $W^{-1}(1_P\otimes u)$ corresponds to $1_{W^{-1}P}\otimes u$, which is therefore injective. Hence $W^{-1}P$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, line 23921): 'as the localization of a flat module is flat'; used implicitly in the last sentence of the Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), proof

proof.text: (Claim P: flatness passes along a base change followed by a localization.) Let $A\to A'$ and $A\to B$ be ring maps, $B'$ a ring with ring maps $B\to B'$ and $A'\to B'$ agreeing on $A$, such that the induced map $C:=B\otimes_AA'\to B'$, $b\otimes a'\mapsto\bar b\,\bar a'$, is a localization of $C$ at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq C$. Let $N$ be a $B$-module which is flat as an $A$-module and $N'$ a $B'$-module ($A'$ acting through $A'\to B'$) with a $B$-linear map $N\to N'$ such that $N\otimes_BB'\to N'$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\bar x$, is an isomorphism. Then $N'$ is a flat $A'$-module. Proof: $P:=N\otimes_AA'$ is a $C$-module ($(b\otimes a')(x\otimes a'')=bx\otimes a'a''$) and a flat $A'$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. By associativity of the tensor product, $N\otimes_BC\cong P$ ($x\otimes(b\otimes a')\mapsto bx\otimes a'$) and $N\otimes_BB'\cong(N\otimes_BC)\otimes_CB'\cong P\otimes_CB'$, $C$-linearly. Since $C\to B'$ is a localization at $W$, $B'\cong W^{-1}C$ as $C$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (its first sentence), and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with the identity ring map of $C$, $T=W$, the $C$-module $C$ and the $C$-module $P$) gives $W^{-1}C\otimes_CP\cong W^{-1}P$. Hence $N'\cong W^{-1}P$ as $C$-modules, so as $A'$-modules, since $A'\to C\to B'$ is the given map $A'\to B'$. By Claim L (step 1, with $A'\to C$, $W$ and $P$), $W^{-1}P$, hence $N'$, is flat over $A'$.

proof.text: (The limit system.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-tower-essentially-finite-presentation] to $R\to S\to S'$ and $M$, which is allowed by hypotheses (1), (2) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. We obtain a nonempty directed set $\Lambda$, local rings $(R_\lambda,\mathfrak p_\lambda)$, $S_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$ with local homomorphisms $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$, local transition maps, $S'_\lambda$-modules $M_\lambda$ and maps to $R,S,S',M$ with properties (1)-(5) of that node. Since $R_\lambda\to R$ is a local homomorphism of local rings, $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R$ (the inverse image is a proper ideal containing the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p_\lambda$); likewise $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak p_\mu$ under $R_\lambda\to R_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$.

proof.text: (Noetherian local stages.) The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (every ideal is $n\mathbf Z$). If $T_0$ is a Noetherian ring and $T_1$ is essentially of finite type over $T_0$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], i.e. $T_1\cong W^{-1}B$ with $B$ of finite type over $T_0$, then $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and $W^{-1}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Applying this three times with property (2) of step 3: $R_\lambda$, $S_\lambda$ and $S'_\lambda$ are Noetherian local rings. Put $\hat S_\lambda=S_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda$, $\hat S'_\lambda=S'_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda S'_\lambda$ and $\hat M_\lambda=M_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda M_\lambda$. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]; they are local, because $\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{S_\lambda}$ ($R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ is local), so $\hat S_\lambda\ne0$ and its ideals not containing $1$ lie in $\mathfrak m_{S_\lambda}/\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda$ (same for $S'_\lambda$). The maps $S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$, $S_\lambda\to S_\mu$, $S'_\lambda\to S'_\mu$, $M_\lambda\to M_\mu$ ($\lambda\le\mu$) pass to the quotients, since $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ maps into $\mathfrak p_\mu$ (step 3), and the induced ring maps $\hat S_\lambda\to\hat S'_\lambda$, $\hat S_\lambda\to\hat S_\mu$, $\hat S'_\lambda\to\hat S'_\mu$ are local homomorphisms; $\hat M_\lambda$ is a finitely generated $\hat S'_\lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (images of generators of $M_\lambda$, property (3)).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), proof; Noetherianity is what Lemma 00MP needs of $R_\lambda$, $S_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$ (from 'essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$' by Lemma Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence)

proof.text: ($S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization.) Let $\lambda\le\mu$ and $E=S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$. By associativity of the tensor product, $S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\cong S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}E$. By property (4) of step 3, $E\to S_\mu$ is a localization at some $W\subseteq E$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with the ring map $E\to D:=S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}E$), $D\to D\otimes_ES_\mu\cong S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu$ is a localization at the image of $W$; and $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization by property (4). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (1) the composite $S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S'_\mu$, which is $x\otimes a\mapsto\bar x\,\bar a$, is a localization at a multiplicative subset.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), proof, second paragraph: 'This also implies that $S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization'

proof.text: ($M_\lambda$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ for $\lambda$ large.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] to the system $A_\lambda=R_\lambda$, $B_\lambda=S'_\lambda$ (with the local homomorphism $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$), $N_\lambda=M_\lambda$: the rings are Noetherian local (step 4), the transition maps local (step 3), $M_\lambda$ is finitely generated (property (3)), hypothesis (a) holds by step 5 and (b) by property (4); by property (1) the colimits are $A=R$, $B=S'$ with the map $\beta\circ\alpha$, and $N=M$ with its $S'$-module structure. Since $M$ is flat over $R$ (hypothesis (5)), there is $\lambda_0$ with $M_{\lambda_0}$ flat over $R_{\lambda_0}$. For $\mu\ge\lambda_0$, step 2 (Claim P) with $A=R_{\lambda_0}$, $A'=R_\mu$, $B=S'_{\lambda_0}$, $B'=S'_\mu$, $N=M_{\lambda_0}$, $N'=M_\mu$ (hypotheses by step 5 and property (4)) shows that $M_\mu$ is flat over $R_\mu$.

(The fibre system.) (i) For $\lambda\le\mu$ the map $\hat S'_\lambda\otimes_{\hat S_\lambda}\hat S_\mu	o\hat S'_\mu$ is a localization and $\hat M_\lambda\otimes_{\hat S'_\lambda}\hat S'_\mu	o\hat M_\mu$ is an isomorphism (notation of step 4). proof.text: ($\hat M_\lambda$ is flat over $\hat S_\lambda$ for $\lambda$ large.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] to the system $A_\lambda=\hat S_\lambda$, $B_\lambda=\hat S'_\lambda$, $N_\lambda=\hat M_\lambda$: Noetherian local rings, local maps and finitely generated modules by step 4; hypotheses (a), (b) by step 7 (i); colimits $A=S/\mathfrak mS$, $B=S'/\mathfrak mS'$, $N=M/\mathfrak mM$ by step 7 (ii). Since $M/\mathfrak mM$ is flat over $S/\mathfrak mS$ (hypothesis (4)), there is $\lambda_1$ with $\hat M_{\lambda_1}$ flat over $\hat S_{\lambda_1}$. For $\mu\ge\lambda_1$, step 2 (Claim P) with $A=\hat S_{\lambda_1}$, $A'=\hat S_\mu$, $B=\hat S'_{\lambda_1}$, $B'=\hat S'_\mu$, $N=\hat M_{\lambda_1}$, $N'=\hat M_\mu$ (hypotheses by step 7 (i)) shows that $\hat M_\mu$ is flat over $\hat S_\mu$.

proof.text: (The Noetherian case at one stage.) As $\Lambda$ is directed, choose $\lambda\ge\lambda_0,\lambda_1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] (Stacks 00MP) to the local homomorphisms of Noetherian local rings $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$ (step 4) and the $S'_\lambda$-module $M_\lambda$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ of $R_\lambda$: (1) $M_\lambda$ is finitely generated (property (3)); (2) $M_\lambda\ne0$, for otherwise $M\cong M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'=0$ (property (5)), contradicting hypothesis (3); (3) $M_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda M_\lambda=\hat M_\lambda$ is flat over $S_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda=\hat S_\lambda$ (step 8); (4) $M_\lambda$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ (step 6). Hence $S_\lambda$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ and $M_\lambda$ is a flat $S_\lambda$-module.

proof.text: ($S$ is flat over $R$.) Apply step 2 (Claim P) with $A=R_\lambda$, $A'=R$, $B=S_\lambda$, $B'=S$ (the maps $S_\lambda\to S$ and $\alpha:R\to S$ agree on $R_\lambda$), $N=S_\lambda$, flat over $R_\lambda$ by step 9, and $N'=S$ with the map $S_\lambda\to S$ ($S_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to S$ is the canonical isomorphism). Its hypothesis that $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$ is a localization is property (5) of step 3 [lem-weil-pbc-limit-tower-essentially-finite-presentation]. Hence $S$ is a flat $R$-module, i.e. $\alpha$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: ($M$ is flat over $S$.) Apply step 2 (Claim P) with $A=S_\lambda$, $A'=S$, $B=S'_\lambda$, $B'=S'$ (the maps $S'_\lambda\to S'$ and $\beta$ agree on $S_\lambda$), $N=M_\lambda$, flat over $S_\lambda$ by step 9, and $N'=M$ with the map $M_\lambda\to M$; its hypotheses, that $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to S'$ is a localization and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'\to M$ an isomorphism, are property (5) of step 3 [lem-weil-pbc-limit-tower-essentially-finite-presentation]. Hence $M$, an $S$-module through $\beta$, is a flat $S$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].
